issues.where: d5 Primary Care Referral Note (release: start)
issues.problem: This start-released referral note states 'Family history of RF-positive RA in mother with hand deformities' and effectively states the suspected diagnosis category before the learner does any work, duplicating fact f6 but as a chart artifact available at start rather than something the patient reveals in interview. Since f6 is tagged tier 'initial' (volunteered), this is partially consistent, but combined with the note's phrasing it strongly pre-frames the diagnosis as RA for the learner before any history or labs are taken, undermining the diagnostic reasoning objective (o2). Consider softening the note to omit the explicit 'RF-positive' qualifier and let serology be the learner's own discovery under a1-a9, or keep family history mention but strip the implied diagnostic conclusion.

issues.where: a14 Review medication list -> objective o4 factIds f20, f21, f34
issues.problem: Action a14 'Review medication list' is only linked to artifact d2 (which lists only ibuprofen and prenatal vitamin, with no mention of herbal supplement or pregnancy intention), yet objective o4 maps this single record-review action to critical/important reluctant facts f20 (herbal supplement) and f21 (pregnancy intention) and reluctant f34 (herbal details). These are reluctant/hidden facts that must be elicited via direct, sensitive questioning in the interview, not via a passive record review action. As written, the medication list artifact does not contain the herbal supplement or pregnancy-intention information (confirmed by d2's table), so the objective-to-action mapping is inconsistent with the artifact itself and could mislead case design/scoring - no actual leak in the artifact content, but the mapping overstates what a14 reveals. Fix the objective mapping to rely on interview facts only, not a14.

The action is labeled 'Calculate DAS28 / joint count assessment' but the result only reports raw tender/swollen joint counts (10 tender, 8 swollen) without any CRP or ESR incorporation to actually compute a DAS28 score, and without reporting a composite numeric DAS28 value. Either rename the action to 'Joint count assessment' only, or show the actual DAS28-CRP calculation using TJC28, SJC28, CRP, and patient global assessment to produce a numeric score (e.g., DAS28-CRP ~5.1, indicating high disease activity) for internal consistency with the action name.

DAS28 uses a 28-joint count (MCPs, PIPs, wrists, elbows, shoulders, knees) and does not include MTPs. The case reports tender/swollen counts that include MTPs (bilateral MTP squeeze test positive, a2/a4), which are not part of the standard 28-joint set. If DAS28 is to be calculated, MTP findings should be excluded from the 28-joint count or the assessment should be relabeled to avoid implying a true DAS28 score includes forefoot joints.

issues.where: a16 result vs d4 diary data
issues.problem: a16 result states 'morning stiffness averaging 85-100 minutes daily' but the d4 chart data points are 90, 95, 80, 100, 90, 85, 95 (average ≈90.7, range 80-100), so the lower bound of 85 is understated compared to the actual data minimum of 80. Adjust wording to 'averaging about 90 minutes, ranging 80-100 minutes' for accuracy.
